Incidence-Matrix Diagnostics

Muhammad Yaseen

2026-09-26

Source: vignettes/ppgt_diagnostics.qmd

1 Abstract

This vignette develops two matrix diagnostics that are useful across the whole package:

  • pool overlap through \(\mathbf{M}\mathbf{M}^\top\)
  • sample co-occurrence through \(\mathbf{M}^\top\mathbf{M}\)

These diagnostics are presented as vignette material only. They are not new exported package helpers.

They also sit outside the constructor, decoder, simulation, and workflow APIs. The matrices \(\mathbf{M}\mathbf{M}^\top\) and \(\mathbf{M}^\top\mathbf{M}\) are interpretive summaries of a fixed design \(\mathbf{M}\); they do not choose a decoder, execute retesting, or implement stage-2 protocol logic.

2 Architecture Boundary

Within the package layer model:

  1. construction returns \(\mathbf{M}\)
  2. decoding interprets \(\mathbf{z}\) relative to \(\mathbf{M}\)
  3. simulation generates \(\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}\) and \(\mathbf{z}\)
  4. workflow execution coordinates stage-1 and optional stage-2 logic
  5. reporting summarizes stored workflow objects

The diagnostics in this article belong to none of those execution layers. They are read-only summaries of a fixed incidence matrix.

3 Pool-Overlap Matrix

For \(\mathbf{M} \in \{0,1\}^{J \times N}\), the pool-overlap matrix is \(\mathbf{M}\mathbf{M}^\top = \operatorname{tcrossprod}(\mathbf{M})\).

The \((j, j')\) entry counts how many individuals belong to both \(\mathcal{P}_j\) and \(\mathcal{P}_{j'}\). The diagonal entries are the pool sizes \(n_j\).

More explicitly, \[ (\mathbf{M}\mathbf{M}^\top)_{jj'} = \sum_{i=1}^N M_{ji} M_{j'i} = |\mathcal{P}_j \cap \mathcal{P}_{j'}|. \]

M_pp <- pp_matrix(q = 4, d = 3, nl = 5)
M_pp

4 Sample Co-Occurrence Matrix

The sample co-occurrence matrix is \(\mathbf{M}^\top \mathbf{M} = \operatorname{crossprod}(\mathbf{M})\).

The \((i, i')\) entry counts how many pools contain both individuals \(i\) and \(i'\). The diagonal entries are the sample coverages \(w_i\).

Equivalently, \[ (\mathbf{M}^\top \mathbf{M})_{ii'} = \sum_{j=1}^J M_{ji} M_{ji'} = |\mathcal{J}_i \cap \mathcal{J}_{i'}|. \]

sample_overlap <- Matrix::crossprod(M_pp)
sample_overlap

5 Gramian Identities And Design Interpretation

The two diagnostics can be read as exact Gramian identities: \[ \mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{pool}} = \mathbf{M}\mathbf{M}^\top, \qquad \mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{sample}} = \mathbf{M}^\top\mathbf{M}. \] Their diagonal entries recover the canonical row and column weights, \[ (\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{pool}})_{jj} = n_j, \qquad (\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{sample}})_{ii} = w_i, \] while their off-diagonal entries recover pairwise overlaps, \[ (\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{pool}})_{jj'} = |\mathcal{P}_j \cap \mathcal{P}_{j'}|, \qquad (\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{sample}})_{ii'} = |\mathcal{J}_i \cap \mathcal{J}_{i'}|. \] This viewpoint is useful across all design families because it turns qualitative balance and overlap questions into direct matrix identities.

6 Why These Diagnostics Matter

These matrices help interpret several design properties.

  • Balance: the diagonals of \(\mathbf{M}\mathbf{M}^\top\) and \(\mathbf{M}^\top\mathbf{M}\) show whether \(n_j\) and \(w_i\) are constant.
  • Overlap control: the off-diagonal entries show how often pools or individuals intersect.
  • Separable and disjunct behavior: small sample co-occurrence makes it easier for different active sets to induce distinguishable pooled outcomes, and makes it easier for an outside individual to retain a pool that is not covered by a bounded active set.
